title: Felix and the Alibi
premise: Felix Eriksen, a night-shift dispatcher who has spent a decade listening to the city's last calls, takes an anonymous prepaid booking: a client wants proof that a murder scheduled for the upcoming Voss family anniversary dinner has not yet happened. The client is dead by morning, and Felix realizes the 'murder' being prevented may be one committed thirty years ago — a death everyone in the wealthy Voss circle alibied each other out of. As Felix digs through old taxi logs, hospital records, and their own company's buried history, they discover the original victim was a young dispatcher like themselves, erased to protect the family's reputation. At the anniversary dinner, Felix forces the truth into the open, and the surviving conspirators fracture: one confesses, one flees, and the matriarch, Ingrid Voss, admits she paid for the investigation herself, wanting to be caught before she died. Felix, who built a life on being unnoticeable, finally claims a place — among the Voss's estranged granddaughter and the ragtag night-shift crew who become the family they never had.
about_author: Rafael Okafor is a former emergency dispatcher turned novelist who writes mysteries about the people who answer phones in the dark. He lives in Oslo with his partner and a deaf terrier named Static.

chapters.title: The Prepaid Fare
chapters.summary: Felix Eriksen, night dispatcher at Meridian Cabs, receives an odd booking: cash in advance, instructions to verify no murder occurs at the Voss anniversary dinner. POV Felix. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Static on the Line
chapters.summary: The client's callback number leads to a disconnected payphone outside St. Hallvard's Hospital. Felix replays the call, noticing a tremor in the voice. POV Felix. Beat: unease deepening into obsession.

chapters.title: Night Shift Rules
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter to Felix's first year dispatching, establishing mentor Marit and the crew's found-family rituals. POV Felix. Beat: tenderness, showing what Felix stands to lose.

chapters.title: The Voss Name
chapters.summary: Felix researches the Voss shipping dynasty; the thirtieth anniversary dinner commemorates something other than a wedding. A 1994 obituary mentions a cab driver's death. POV Felix. Beat: first cold dread.

chapters.title: Dead Client
chapters.summary: Police notify Meridian that the prepaid account holder, Astrid Holm, was found drowned. Officially an accident. Felix recognizes her voice from the recording. POV Felix. Beat: guilt and fear.

chapters.title: Detective Brandt
chapters.summary: Detective Ivar Brandt interviews Felix, sharp-eyed and skeptical of coincidences. Felix hides the recording, unsure why. POV Felix. Beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Marit's Silence
chapters.summary: Felix asks Marit about 1994; she goes pale and changes the subject, then warns Felix to drop it. POV Felix. Beat: betrayal — the family that protects you can also lie to you.

chapters.title: The Old Logbook
chapters.summary: In the archive basement, Felix finds a gap in the 1994 dispatch logs — three hours cut out with a razor blade. POV Felix. Beat: thrill of discovery shadowed by menace.

chapters.title: Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Nora Voss, estranged heir, comes to book a cab home from her grandmother's estate; she and Felix recognize fellow outsiders. POV Nora. Beat: cautious kinship.

chapters.title: Astrid's Apartment
chapters.summary: Felix breaks into Astrid's flat, finding clippings about the 1994 driver, Tomas Lindqvist, and a photo of five young people including Ingrid Voss. POV Felix. Beat: the past becoming physical.

chapters.title: Five at the Table
chapters.summary: Felix identifies the photo's faces: Ingrid Voss, her late husband, business partner Dahl, family doctor Reinholt, and Marit. POV Felix. Beat: vertigo — everyone Felix trusts was there.

chapters.title: Someone Follows
chapters.summary: A grey sedan tails Felix across the city; they lose it in the docks fog. POV Felix. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Tomas Lindqvist
chapters.summary: Research reveals Tomas died in a hit-and-run weeks after claiming he witnessed something at a Voss party. Case closed in nine days. POV Felix. Beat: grief for a stranger who mirrors them.

chapters.title: Brandt Again
chapters.summary: Brandt reveals Astrid was Ingrid Voss's former secretary; he suspects Felix knows more. Uneasy non-alliance forms. POV alternating Felix/Brandt. Beat: grudging respect.

chapters.title: What Marit Knows
chapters.summary: Confronted gently, Marit admits she drove the cab that night but swears she never saw a body — only that she was paid to forget. POV Marit. Beat: sorrow, loyalty cracking.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Invitation
chapters.summary: A cream envelope arrives at the depot: Ingrid Voss invites Felix personally to the dinner. POV Felix. Beat: trap or invitation? Dread laced with dark humor.

chapters.title: Rehearsal of Lies
chapters.summary: Felix maps each suspect's thirty-year-old alibi against modern records; Dahl's charity gala timestamp doesn't match the weather archives. POV Felix. Beat: methodical hope.

chapters.title: Nora's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Nora shares letters suggesting her grandfather's 'heart attack' followed his discovery of something. She and Felix grow closer over bad coffee. POV Nora. Beat: warmth, belonging budding.

chapters.title: Break-In at the Depot
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks the office searching for the missing log pages; Marit's locker is emptied. The crew closes ranks around Felix. POV Felix. Beat: found family as shield.

chapters.title: Doctor Reinholt
chapters.summary: Felix visits the retired doctor, who babbles about 'the girl in the water' before his nurse cuts the visit short. POV Felix. Beat: horror — there was a second victim.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Water
chapters.summary: Records show an unnamed Jane Doe pulled from the harbor in 1994, cremated unclaimed. Astrid had been investigating her identity. POV Felix. Beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Dahl's Offer
chapters.summary: Business magnate Dahl offers Felix money to hand over Astrid's files and leave town. Felix refuses. POV Felix. Beat: temptation refused; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: The grey sedan runs Felix's bike off the road; bruised, Felix realizes someone inside the conspiracy is panicking. POV Felix. Beat: fear transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: Marit Confesses More
chapters.summary: Marit recalls driving Ingrid home that night, Ingrid soaked to the skin, whispering 'it wasn't supposed to be her.' POV Marit. Beat: devastating partial truth.

chapters.title: Nora Confronts Ingrid
chapters.summary: Nora demands answers from her grandmother and is coldly dismissed; she leaves with a key taken from Ingrid's desk. POV Nora. Beat: rupture between blood and truth.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Key
chapters.summary: The key opens a Voss boathouse containing Tomas's missing logbook pages and Astrid's final notes naming her killer — the page torn away. POV Felix. Beat: so close, then robbed.

chapters.title: Brandt's Cold Case
chapters.summary: Felix brings Brandt the evidence; he reopens the Lindqvist file quietly, warning Felix the dinner is two days away. POV Brandt. Beat: alliance solidifying.

chapters.title: Suspect Math
chapters.summary: Felix deduces the torn page's owner must have had access to both Astrid and the boathouse: only Ingrid or her caretaker, Sander. POV Felix. Beat: narrowing dread.

chapters.title: Sander
chapters.summary: The caretaker Sander, silent for decades, tells Felix he saw Ingrid strike the girl — and that Astrid came to him frightened, certain Ingrid knew she knew. POV Sander. Beat: witness testimony, heavy as stone.

chapters.title: Why Felix
chapters.summary: Felix realizes why the booking went to Meridian: Astrid trusted the one company whose dispatcher once tried to help Tomas. It was meant for Marit. POV Felix. Beat: inheritance of unfinished justice.

chapters.title: Eve of the Dinner
chapters.summary: Preparations at Voss House; Felix watches staff polish silver over old sins. A threatening note appears under their door: 'Some fares are one-way.' POV Felix. Beat: calm before catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: At the dinner, Ingrid raises a glass to 'thirty years of keeping faith.' Felix, seated among guests, catches Dahl slipping something into his pocket. POV Felix. Beat: suffocating tension.

chapters.title: Lights Out
chapters.summary: The power fails; in the dark, a shot rings out. When lights return, Dahl lies bleeding and Sander is gone. POV Felix. Beat: chaos, the plan collapsing.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Trapped by storm-closed gates, Felix organizes the household, using dispatcher skills to triage and keep order while Brandt races through the rain. POV Felix. Beat: competence as courage.

chapters.title: Ingrid's Parlor
chapters.summary: Ingrid privately confesses everything to Felix: the girl was her husband's mistress, the killing half-accident, the cover-up deliberate. She hired Astrid hoping to be stopped. POV Ingrid. Beat: chilling, humanizing ruin.

chapters.title: Sander Returns
chapters.summary: Sander, revealed as the shooter protecting Ingrid from Dahl's blackmail, surrenders to Brandt; Dahl survives and will trade testimony for immunity. POV Brandt. Beat: justice arriving imperfectly.

chapters.title: The Reading of Names
chapters.summary: Before police statements, Felix reads aloud the names of Tomas and the Jane Doe — now identified as Lene Bakke — at the dinner table. POV Felix. Beat: mourning made public; catharsis.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Arrests, headlines, Marit retiring in peace after testifying. Felix declines Ingrid's money but accepts her apology. POV Felix. Beat: exhaustion and release.

chapters.title: New Routes
chapters.summary: Weeks later: Felix trains a new dispatcher, Nora visits the depot with coffee, Brandt sends case updates. Small rituals rebuilt. POV Felix. Beat: quiet joy, belonging earned.

chapters.title: The Last Call
chapters.summary: On the anniversary of Tomas's death, Felix drives the route of his final fare alone, then answers the night line: 'Meridian Cabs, where to?' POV Felix. Beat: resolution — invisible no longer, home at last.
